rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Relative error is about 1 part in the first uncertain digit.
Percentage error = relative error × 100%

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A precise instrument can be wrong if it is not calibrated.  ·  Leading zeros in 0.0025 are not significant. That number has two significant figures.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 0.00250 has three significant figures because the last zero is after the decimal and after a non-zero digit.  ·  A systematic error shifts all readings the same way and hurts accuracy.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Accuracy describes how close a measurement is to the accepted true value. Precision describes how close repeated measurements are to each other. A set of readings can be precise and still inaccurate if the instrument has a systematic offset.  ·  Significant figures are the digits that carry meaning in a measured number. Leading zeros in a decimal only locate the point and are not significant. Zeros between non-zero digits are significant. Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Addition follows decimal places. Multiplication follows significant figures. They are different rules.  ·  An exact 2 in 2as is not a measured 2.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: In multiplication and division, the result is quoted with as many significant figures as the least precise factor. In addition and subtraction, the result is limited by the last decimal place that all terms share.  ·  Exact counted numbers, such as 2 in the formula 2πr, are not measured data. They do not limit the significant figures. A given radius of 1.20 m does.  ·  Scientific notation makes the significant figures obvious. 1.20 × 10^3 m has three significant figures. Writing 1200 m does not, unless extra information says the zeros are significant.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Rounding  ·  The answer cannot be more precise than the data.  ·  Precision, Accuracy & Significant Figures is based on fundamental principles.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Do not write a calculator's ten digits as the answer.  ·  State the unit with the rounded number.  ·  Round once, at the end.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write Relative error is about 1 part in the first uncertain digit. and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Rounding is done at the end of a calculation, not after every intermediate line, so that rounding error does not pile up. The final line should still not pretend to more digits than the data allow.
